assumptions: The family installer permits process observation and pilot recruitment without exposing unconsented beneficiary data.
A material share of packs contain preventable defects or consume enough installer time to justify a 500-1,200 PLN fee.
The business limits regulated advice appropriately and can secure qualified escalation support.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Ten or more permissioned cases measuring baseline defects, avoided resubmissions, turnaround and payer behavior, followed by paid repeat orders from independent installers with verified contribution margin and referral CAC.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: Positioning immediately before reimbursement submission connects document QA to a concrete cash-unlock event and supports per-case charging.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Defective packs can delay materially larger beneficiary or installer payments, giving a credible value basis, but defect frequency and actual payment behavior are not measured.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Low referral CAC, per-case cash conversion, and a manual-to-automation path are credible; margins remain reviewer-dependent and the 6,000-case wealth path, throughput, repeat volume, and program longevity are assumptions.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Installers repeatedly handling Czyste Powietrze projects form a narrow reachable segment, though annual eligible case volume and market durability are unknown.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: Fast standardized closeout and installer integration could win a regional niche, but auditors, consultants, and installers can bundle the service and access is nonexclusive.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: The workflow can extend to other retrofit grants, financing closeouts, energy documentation, and installer back-office services, subject to program-specific rules.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: A defect taxonomy and reviewer playbooks improve operations, but they are copyable and the core family access is revocable, nontransferable, and replaceable.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: Turnaround and reduced rejection risk can be visibly valuable compared with self-service, although no observed error reduction or approval acceleration is supplied.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: Payment applications create current recurring events, but policy changes can rapidly alter volume, forms, or economics.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: Permissioned observation through the family installer offers an unusually practical validation route, followed by installer, accountant, and auditor referrals; broader repeatability is still unproven.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: Ten manual packs can be tested cheaply alongside employment, but reviewer accuracy, credentials, GDPR controls, liability, and scaling case labor require disciplined operations.

highest_value_structural_change: Convert the family-workflow access into a standardized, permissioned pilot and then secure multi-installer framework contracts with recurring case minimums and outcome tracking.
main_structural_strength: The founder has a low-cost route to observe and validate a workflow directly tied to subsidy payment, enabling service revenue before software investment.
primary_score_limiter: The scalable case volume, defect rate, permissible service scope, and independence from reviewer labor and one changing subsidy program are unknown.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Beneficiaries can complete applications themselves, and program changes could sharply reduce volumes or obsolete the workflow.
